- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥15 days), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 3–5% of forecasted range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 periods.
- If recent 3–5-day true values show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 45.0), model overreacts; dampen forecast slope toward prior 10-day average.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., +1.00 after -1.00), model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–4% to capture sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true values after 10–15 day lag; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for lagged events.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 2+ consecutive days, model exhibits “overconfidence bias”; reduce next forecast by 5–8% to avoid runaway momentum.
